errors.quote: one that binds allosterically (non-competitive/uncompetitive target inhibition)
errors.issue: Kinetic class is not a binding-site map: allosteric inhibitors can show competitive patterns, and noncompetitive/uncompetitive kinetics alone do not establish allosteric binding.

errors.quote: The $R^2$ for the non-linear regression models in Phase 3 must be >0.90 to confidently classify the inhibition mechanism.
errors.issue: A high fit R-squared does not distinguish competing kinetic models or establish parameter identifiability. Compare global models with residuals, uncertainty and adequate substrate/inhibitor ranges.

errors.quote: a fixed concentration of the pure, pre-generated final fluorophore
errors.issue: A correction from one fluorophore concentration is not validated over the product range. Chemical fluorophore changes, reporter substrate effects and condition-dependent attenuation can persist.

The design does not establish independent preparations/days, replication sufficient for precision, or a nested analysis. Automated extraction also does not substitute for blinded/predefined analysis decisions.

errors.quote: If Phase 2 reveals the compound inhibits the reporter enzyme >50%
errors.issue: This threshold is not an identifying boundary. Smaller reporter effects can materially bias the coupled rate; orthogonal target validation and reporter-capacity checks at relevant conditions are needed, with chemical substrate/product controls.

rationale: Clear short plan with the right broad counterassays and initial-rate matrix. It conflates kinetic class with binding location, treats model fit quality as mechanism confidence, and leaves correction validation, independent replication and direct product analysis underdeveloped.
reference_guardrails: D3 establishes spectral proximity, not the magnitude of inner filtering. Fluorophore-only signal loss does not distinguish absorption, quenching and chemical conversion.
Substrate-competitive inhibition is a kinetic subclass of target inhibition; it is not necessarily active-site occupancy. Substrate sequestration and chemical loss require separate controls.
Reporter-only inhibition and true target inhibition can coexist. Do not force mutually exclusive categories or subtract arbitrary effect percentages.

A fully validated staged reporter calibration can be informative; a specific analytical instrument is not mandatory. Target quenching, matrix matching, product recovery and chemical stability must justify the inference.
Orthogonal methods can have their own compound-dependent artifacts, including ion suppression. Nonfluorescence alone does not establish specificity.
Independent preparations/days support reproducibility; technical wells cannot substitute for them. A null significance test is not equivalence; margins should be scientifically justified.
Simple inner-filter correction formulas depend on optical geometry. For f=F_without/F_with, attenuation correction multiplies signal by f, not by 1/f.

The draft reference uses reporter Km as a preparation item, but full reporter Michaelis-Menten characterization is not universally essential if empirical capacity and relevant intermediate concentrations are validated.

No fixed concentrations, replicate counts, Z-prime or R-squared thresholds are supplied by the packet. Proposed pilot settings are acceptable when labeled and validated; they are not historical facts.
